$comment: SWAP LAYER — the binding to your test-management system (<TMS_NAME>). Ids only, no secrets —
safe to commit. TMS_TOKEN lives in .env (gitignored). Refresh ids with: npm run tms:resolve
The field NAMES here are generic concepts every TMS has in some form: a project, a root folder
that roots the component tree, a case template, the case content fields, and the mechanism that
links a case to an issue. The exact shape (custom-field prefixes, dropdown value-ids, step
columns) is TMS-specific — record yours under `caseFields` and `notes`.
READ THE ID TRAP. Many TMS UIs put an id in the URL that is NOT the id the API wants (a project
id where the path segment reads like a repository id, a folder id in a query param). Resolving
by the wrong id lands on a real but WRONG project and looks like success. Resolve by NAME, and
make `tms-resolve.ts` refuse to guess.
rootFolderNote: The folder that roots <PRODUCT_NAME>'s component tree — the write target for the skills.
templateNote: If this template is shared across products, the case standard bends to the template rather than the reverse — editing a shared template changes every team's case editor.

$comment: Map the framework's canonical case fields onto whatever your TMS calls them. Set a field to
null when it genuinely does not exist on your template, and note what you do instead — e.g.
carry Type as a TAG when there is no Type field. A null with an explanation is a decision; a
missing key is a question. If your TMS namespaces custom fields (a prefix, an id), keep that
exact string here — a create call against a field absent from the template usually fails.
caseFields.typeNote: If no Type field exists, carry Smoke/Functional/Regression/Negative/Edge Case as a TAG. Do not invent a field.

dropdownValues.$comment: Many TMS dropdowns take a VALUE ID, not the label. Fill from `npm run tms:resolve` or admin.

$comment: How a case links to its tracker issue. Two mechanisms exist across TMS products and they are
NOT interchangeable — pick the one YOUR instance actually supports and VERIFY it once:
'native'  — a first-class issue field/array on the case (needs a tracker integration set up)
'tag'     — a key-shaped tag on the case (when no integration exists)
The failure this prevents: a link written the UNSUPPORTED way appears to succeed and is
invisible to every query, including the regression run's. NEVER put the key in a plain custom
text field — invisible under either mechanism.
Binding for submitting automated results. Results map to cases by the @C<caseId> tag carried
in the TEST TITLE — most runners' separate `tag` option does not reach the machine-readable
test name your TMS matches on, which is why the tag lives in the title string.
automation.issueTagPatternNote: Deliberately matches ANY uppercase-prefix key, not one project. A narrow pattern drops keys silently — the @C<id> tag still maps the result, so the run looks complete while the issue link is simply absent. Widen rather than replace when a tracker changes.
